title: Intelligence Theories: Thurstone, Gardner, Sternberg, PASS
summary: Primary Mental Abilities (Thurstone), Structure of Intellect (Guilford), Multiple Intelligences (Gardner), Triarchic Theory (Sternberg), PASS Theory (Das, Naglieri, Kirby).
objectives: List Thurstone's seven primary mental abilities.
revision: Thurstone: 7 primary mental abilities. Gardner: 8 intelligences. Sternberg: 3 types (analytical, creative, practical). PASS: Planning, Attention, Simultaneous, Successive.
traps: Gardner proposed eight intelligences (originally seven, later added naturalist).
confusions: Confusing Gardner's intelligences with learning styles.

notes.t: Louis Thurstone proposed seven primary mental abilities: verbal comprehension, word fluency, number facility, spatial visualization, associative memory, perceptual speed, and reasoning.
Howard Gardner proposed eight intelligences: linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal, and naturalist.
Robert Sternberg proposed three types of intelligence: analytical (componential), creative (experiential), and practical (contextual).
Das, Naglieri, and Kirby proposed PASS Theory: Planning, Attention, Simultaneous, and Successive processing.
Guilford's SI model proposes 150 different abilities based on operations, contents, and products dimensions.
UGC NET frequently asks about Gardner's eight intelligences, Sternberg's triarchic theory, and PASS theory components.
